summary: Admin AI Platform (P1) tested end-to-end. 29/31 pytest integration tests pass. All admin authorization, dashboard, models/toggle/ping, routing/capability-rejection, translate, embed, review-queue listing, and student regressions pass. Frontend admin UI loads correctly for the admin (dashboard + Models/Routing/Jobs/Usage/Review all render) and is correctly hidden for the student. CRITICAL BACKEND BUG: vocabulary_generation jobs FAIL on topic foreign-key constraint ('Textual studies' not in topics table) — no new REVIEW words are created, blocking the full REVIEW → publish/regenerate workflow. Minor: AI-coach response is wrapped as {content: {...}} but spec said returns {explanation, example, mnemonic} at top level — frontend already uses .content so it works end-to-end, but the shape differs from the problem statement.

critical.issue: Job FAILS with FK violation when AI returns a topic that does not exist in the topics table. Example error: 'insert or update on table "words" violates foreign key constraint "words_topic_fkey". Key (topic)=(Textual studies) is not present in table "topics".' Observed on a C1 'Rare Academic' job (job_d69bf57948ef) — generated_count=0, valid_count=0, status=FAILED. A pre-existing B2 'Academic' job (job_731f6f9cff17) also shows FAILED (0 new, 10 dup, 0 rejected, 10 gen) suggesting ingest routinely rejects AI output. As a consequence, the dashboard shows 'In review: 0' and the REVIEW → publish/reject/archive/regenerate workflow cannot be exercised against freshly generated AI words.
critical.fix_hint: In bulk_ingest / resolve path for AI_GENERATED words, either (a) coerce topic to NULL / fall back to a sentinel 'general' topic when the generated topic is not in exam_slugs/topics, (b) auto-create the missing topic row, or (c) validate at generation step (content_validation) and move the entire word to warnings/REVIEW instead of raising to a FK error. Current content_validation only WARNS on missing topic (content_validation.py:205) — it does not block or coerce unknown topics.

minor.issue: Returns {content:{explanation,example,mnemonic}, provenance, cached} — not {explanation,example,mnemonic} at top level as described in the review request. Frontend already consumes .content so UI works; just note the contract divergence from the spec.

action_items: FIX FK bug in content_ingest for AI_GENERATED words: do not pass an unknown topic to the DB. Either coerce to NULL / 'general', auto-create the topic row, or hard-fail at validation (so the word is dropped with a visible reason) rather than raising the Supabase FK 23503. Verify by re-running POST /api/admin/ai/jobs {count:3,cefr:'C1',topic:'Rare Academic'} and polling until COMPLETED/PARTIAL, then confirm GET /api/admin/vocabulary/review returns new REVIEW words.

After the FK fix, re-run the integration suite (/app/backend/tests/test_admin_ai_platform_integration.py). The 5 skipped review-workflow tests (regenerate/publish/reject/archive) will then execute end-to-end.
Optional: align /api/words/{id}/ai-coach response shape with the spec (flatten content → top-level), or update the review-request documentation to reflect the {content, provenance, cached} wrapper.

rca_of_issue: ROOT CAUSE: content_ingest/bulk_ingest for AI_GENERATED words passes the AI-returned 'topic' string straight to the Supabase insert. The words table has FK 'words_topic_fkey' → topics(slug). content_validation.validate_word only emits a warning for missing topic (content_validation.py:205-206) and never checks membership against the known topics list. When the model returns a plausible-but-unseeded topic (e.g. 'Textual studies'), the insert raises Postgres 23503 which jobs.py catches and marks the entire job FAILED. Reproduction: POST /api/admin/ai/jobs {"count":3,"cefr":"C1","topic":"Rare Academic"} with admin token, then GET /api/admin/ai/jobs/{id} → status=FAILED, error contains 'words_topic_fkey'. Mitigation: (1) in bulk_ingest, resolve topic against repo.get_known_topic_slugs() and set to None/'general' if missing; or (2) extend content_validation to add a hard error (not warning) if topic ∉ known_topics so the word is dropped before DB write; or (3) auto-create missing topic rows (lowest friction but may litter the taxonomy).
